newsitem.title: NETHERLANDS: NWE oil products dip, but demand raises fuel oil.
newsitem.headline: NWE oil products dip, but demand raises fuel oil.

text.p: NWE oil products dipped on Tuesday morning after further crude falls late on Monday, except for fuel oil barges which rose as end-user demand picked up, dealers said.
Gasoline was around $1 a tonne lower. April Eurograde deliveries were discussed at around $189/$191 fob Rotterdam. The dip still left margins better than on Monday.
Regular barges were more settled after deals towards the close on Monday which were $5 apart. Bids were at around $182 fob for prompt deliveries.
Heating oil barges were very slightly lower as IPE gas oil futures dipped. Offers for prompt deliveries held at around April IPE +50 cents.
Meanwhile, one trading house sold 10,000 tonnes of heating oil for second half April to four different buyers, all deals at April +50 cents fob Rotterdam.
High sulphur fuel oil barges traded in the range $83.75 to $84.50, a gain of about $1 a tonne on Monday's close. Dealers said an improvement in the bunker market was behind the slight improvement.
